describe: A branching story: scenes with 2 or 3 choices each. The scene is `scene` (starts at 0); the fragment draws its text and one button per choice and reads the story from four string lists the game declares as state (usually `"init": "content_<key>"`, so all words live in `content`). Encoding: `story_lines` has 4 entries per scene (lines of the scene text, at most about 30 characters each; '' for unused lines), so scene s uses indices s*4 to s*4+3. `story_labels` has 3 entries per scene (button labels, '' for no choice), index s*3+c. `story_next` has 3 entries per scene, index s*3+c, each the number of the scene that choice leads to, written as a string of digits ('7'; scenes 0 to 59). `story_ends` has 1 entry per scene: '' for a normal scene, 'good' or 'bad' for an ending (an ending scene's choices are ignored). Choosing emits `choice_made {scene, choice}` (scene is the scene the choice was made in, choice is 0 to 2; `scene` already holds the new scene when it fires), then, if that scene is an ending, `ending_reached {good}`. With `good_wins` a good ending wins; with `bad_loses` a bad ending loses. Choices are ignored for `read_ms` after each scene appears, so people can read it. Wrong lengths in the lists make choices silently do nothing, so keep them in step. Provides `scene`, `choose` (input) and the events above. With the game's `scene` sprite it draws a picture between the text and the buttons (frame = scene), and with a `button` sprite the buttons draw it.

scene.describe: A picture for the scene, centred at (180, picture_y) and picture_h tall (at most 300 wide). Give svg as a list for one picture per scene (frame = scene number, wrapping around), or one picture for the whole story; `picture_sway` rocks it gently by that many degrees.

button.describe: A choice button, 300 × 52, drawn under the choice text (keep its middle calm).

rules.when: not _ended and now >= _ready_at and event.choice >= 0 and event.choice < 3 and get_or(story_labels, scene * 3 + event.choice, '') != ''

let.target: index_of(map(range(60), n => str(n)), get_or(story_next, scene * 3 + event.choice, ''))

feedback.when: (event.good and not @good_wins) or (not event.good and not @bad_loses)
